notes: Three muṇḍakas, six khaṇḍas, 65 mantras: the lower and the higher knowledge, the rites and their limit; the imperishable from which all comes forth, and the bow of Om; the two birds, the means to the Self, and the knower who becomes Brahman. Meanings and translation follow Śaṅkara's bhāṣya.

words.meaning: O you who are worthy of worship

grammar.en: past active participle m. nom. pl.

invocation.translation: Om. May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O you who are worthy of worship. Praising you with firm limbs and bodies, may we attain the life that the gods have appointed. May Indra of great fame grant us well-being; may Pūṣan who knows all grant us well-being; may Tārkṣya of the unharmed wheel-rim grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati grant us well-being. Om. Peace, peace, peace.
notes: The peace invocation of the Upaniṣads of the Atharvaveda. The 1910 edition does not print it with the Muṇḍaka; the text is that of the GRETIL Praśnopaniṣad, as on the Praśna page. Śaṅkara's bhāṣya does not comment on it; the translation gives the plain sense of the words.

sanskrit.deva:
ब्रह्मा देवानां प्रथमः संबभूव विश्वस्य कर्ता भुवनस्य गोप्ता ।
स ब्रह्मविद्यां सर्वविद्याप्रतिष्ठामथर्वाय ज्येष्ठपुत्राय प्राह ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
brahmā devānāṃ prathamaḥ saṃbabhūva viśvasya kartā bhuvanasya goptā |
sa brahmavidyāṃ sarvavidyāpratiṣṭhām atharvāya jyeṣṭhaputrāya prāha || 1 ||

lines.iast: brahmā devānāṃ prathamaḥ saṃbabhūva viśvasya kartā bhuvanasya goptā
lines.deva: ब्रह्मा देवानां प्रथमः संबभूव विश्वस्य कर्ता भुवनस्य गोप्ता

lines.iast: sa brahmavidyāṃ sarvavidyāpratiṣṭhām atharvāya jyeṣṭhaputrāya prāha
lines.deva: स ब्रह्मविद्यां सर्वविद्याप्रतिष्ठामथर्वाय ज्येष्ठपुत्राय प्राह

padaccheda.iast: brahmā devānām prathamaḥ saṃbabhūva viśvasya kartā bhuvanasya goptā saḥ brahma-vidyām sarva-vidyā-pratiṣṭhām atharvāya jyeṣṭha-putrāya prāha
padaccheda.deva: ब्रह्मा देवानाम् प्रथमः संबभूव विश्वस्य कर्ता भुवनस्य गोप्ता सः ब्रह्म-विद्याम् सर्व-विद्या-प्रतिष्ठाम् अथर्वाय ज्येष्ठ-पुत्राय प्राह

translations.text: Brahmā came into being first among the gods, the maker of the universe, the protector of the world. He taught the knowledge of Brahman, the support of all knowledge, to Atharvan, his eldest son.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the Upaniṣad: at the start the Upaniṣad itself states its relation, the line of teachers who handed the knowledge down, in order to praise it: so great are those by whom it was gained with effort, as the means to the highest good; praised, it wins the hearer's eagerness. The relation of means and end it states later, ‘the knot of the heart is cut’ (2.2.9). It first shows that the lower knowledge, the Ṛgveda and the rest, which is only injunction and prohibition, does not remove ignorance and the other faults that cause the round of birth and death (1.2.8 and after); then it teaches the knowledge of Brahman, to be gained by the teacher's grace after dispassion toward all that means and ends can win (‘having examined the worlds’, 1.2.12); and it states the fruit more than once: ‘he who knows Brahman becomes Brahman’ (3.2.9), ‘they are all freed, immortal beyond’ (3.2.6).

Śaṅkara, on the same: though men of every stage of life are entitled to knowledge as such, it is the knowledge of Brahman resting on renunciation that is the means to liberation, not knowledge joined with rites; the Upaniṣad shows this by ‘living on alms’ (1.2.11) and ‘by the yoga of renunciation’ (3.2.6). Knowledge and action are also opposed: no rite can be performed, even in a dream, together with the vision of the oneness of Brahman and the Self; and since knowledge has no set time and no fixed occasion, it cannot be confined to a time (leaving the rest for rites). That householders are found handing on this knowledge is a mere mark and cannot overturn what reason has settled: not even a hundred injunctions could put darkness and light in one place, still less mere marks.

Śaṅkara, on the name: it is called upaniṣad because, in those who approach this knowledge of Brahman as their own self, with faith and devotion, it loosens (śātayati) the host of evils, conception, birth, old age, disease; or leads them to the supreme Brahman; or utterly destroys ignorance, the cause of the round of birth and death: so the root sad with upa and ni is remembered to mean.

Śaṅkara: brahmā: the great one, surpassing all others in dharma, knowledge, dispassion and lordship. prathamaḥ: foremost in qualities, or first in time. saṃbabhūva: came forth of his own freedom, not as others are born under the power of dharma and adharma (Manu 1.7). The epithets that follow praise the knowledge through its teacher. brahmavidyā: the knowledge of Brahman, the supreme Self, for it is described as that ‘by which one knows the imperishable Puruṣa’ (1.2.13); or the knowledge told by Brahmā, the first-born. sarvavidyāpratiṣṭhā: the support of all knowledge, because it is the cause by which all knowledge comes forth; or because by it alone what all knowledge knows is known (‘by which the unheard becomes heard’, Chāndogya 6.1.3). jyeṣṭhaputra: among Brahmā's many ways of creating, Atharvan was created first in one of them.

sanskrit.deva:
अथर्वणे यां प्रवदेत ब्रह्माथर्वा तां पुरोवाचाङ्गिरे ब्रह्मविद्याम् ।
स भारद्वाजाय सत्यवहाय प्राह भारद्वाजोऽङ्गिरसे परावराम् ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
atharvaṇe yāṃ pravadeta brahmātharvā tāṃ purovācāṅgire brahmavidyām |
sa bhāradvājāya satyavahāya prāha bhāradvājo 'ṅgirase parāvarām || 2 ||

lines.iast: atharvaṇe yāṃ pravadeta brahmātharvā tāṃ purovācāṅgire brahmavidyām
lines.deva: अथर्वणे यां प्रवदेत ब्रह्माथर्वा तां पुरोवाचाङ्गिरे ब्रह्मविद्याम्

lines.iast: sa bhāradvājāya satyavahāya prāha bhāradvājo 'ṅgirase parāvarām
lines.deva: स भारद्वाजाय सत्यवहाय प्राह भारद्वाजोऽङ्गिरसे परावराम्

padaccheda.iast: atharvaṇe yām pravadeta brahmā atharvā tām purā uvāca aṅgire brahma-vidyām saḥ bhāradvājāya satyavahāya prāha bhāradvājaḥ aṅgirase parāvarām
padaccheda.deva: अथर्वणे याम् प्रवदेत ब्रह्मा अथर्वा ताम् पुरा उवाच अङ्गिरे ब्रह्म-विद्याम् सः भारद्वाजाय सत्यवहाय प्राह भारद्वाजः अङ्गिरसे परावराम्

translations.text: The knowledge of Brahman which Brahmā taught to Atharvan, Atharvan of old told to Aṅgir; he taught it to Satyavaha of the line of Bharadvāja; and Bhāradvāja (taught) to Aṅgiras this (knowledge) handed down from higher to lower.

notes: Śaṅkara: pravadeta stands for the past, prāvadat, ‘taught’. aṅgir: one named Aṅgir. bhāradvāja: of the line (gotra) of Bharadvāja; satyavaha is his name. aṅgirase: to Aṅgiras, his pupil or son. parāvarā: received by each lower from each higher; or reaching over every kind of knowledge, higher and lower. ‘Taught’ is carried over to the last clause.
Many editions read satyavāhāya; the edition and the bhāṣya both read satyavahāya.

sanskrit.deva:
शौनको ह वै महाशालोऽङ्गिरसं विधिवदुपसन्नः पप्रच्छ ।
कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śaunako ha vai mahāśālo 'ṅgirasaṃ vidhivad upasannaḥ papraccha |
kasmin nu bhagavo vijñāte sarvam idaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavatīti || 3 ||

lines.iast: śaunako ha vai mahāśālo 'ṅgirasaṃ vidhivad upasannaḥ papraccha
lines.deva: शौनको ह वै महाशालोऽङ्गिरसं विधिवदुपसन्नः पप्रच्छ

lines.iast: kasmin nu bhagavo vijñāte sarvam idaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavatīti
lines.deva: कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति

padaccheda.iast: śaunakaḥ ha vai mahāśālaḥ aṅgirasam vidhivat upasannaḥ papraccha kasmin nu bhagavaḥ vijñāte sarvam idam vijñātam bhavati iti
padaccheda.deva: शौनकः ह वै महाशालः अङ्गिरसम् विधिवत् उपसन्नः पप्रच्छ कस्मिन् नु भगवः विज्ञाते सर्वम् इदम् विज्ञातम् भवति इति

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle n. loc. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Śaunaka, the great householder, having approached Aṅgiras in due form, asked: ‘Revered sir, what is it which being known, all this becomes known?’

notes: Śaṅkara: Śaunaka, son of Śunaka, a great householder. vidhivat: as the scripture lays down. Since the word is not used of those before Śaunaka and Aṅgiras, it seems that for them the manner of approach was not fixed; the word sets the limit from which it holds; or, like a lamp set in the middle, it lights both ways, for the rule of approach holds for us as well. nu marks doubt. Śaunaka had heard the saying of the wise, ‘when the one is known, one knows all’, and wishing to know what that one is he asked in doubt; or he asked from what is seen in the world, where the many pieces of gold are known by knowing the one gold: is there likewise one cause of all the variety of the world, by knowing which all is known? To the objection that he should first have asked whether there is such a thing, and only then ‘in what’: the question means just that, put shortly to spare words.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मै स होवाच ।
द्वे विद्ये वेदितव्ये इति ह स्म यद्ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति परा चैवापरा च ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmai sa hovāca |
dve vidye veditavye iti ha sma yad brahmavido vadanti parā caivāparā ca || 4 ||

lines.iast: tasmai sa hovāca
lines.deva: तस्मै स होवाच

lines.iast: dve vidye veditavye iti ha sma yad brahmavido vadanti parā caivāparā ca
lines.deva: द्वे विद्ये वेदितव्ये इति ह स्म यद्ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति परा चैवापरा च

padaccheda.iast: tasmai saḥ ha uvāca dve vidye veditavye iti ha sma yat brahma-vidaḥ vadanti parā ca eva aparā ca
padaccheda.deva: तस्मै सः ह उवाच द्वे विद्ये वेदितव्ये इति ह स्म यत् ब्रह्म-विदः वदन्ति परा च एव अपरा च

translations.text: He said to him: ‘Two knowledges are to be known, as those who know Brahman say: the higher and the lower.’

notes: Śaṅkara: brahmavidaḥ: those who know the meaning of the Veda and see the highest truth. parā: the knowledge of the supreme Self; aparā: the knowledge of dharma and adharma, their means and their fruits. Śaunaka asked what, being known, makes one know all, and Aṅgiras speaks of what was not asked; there is no fault, for the answer keeps an order. The lower knowledge is ignorance and must be set aside first, since when its objects are known nothing is known in truth; by the rule that the opposing view is cleared away before the conclusion is stated.

sanskrit.deva:
तत्रापरा ऋग्वेदो यजुर्वेदः सामवेदोऽथर्ववेदः शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं छन्दो ज्योतिषमिति ।
अथ परा यया तदक्षरमधिगम्यते ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tatrāparā ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvavedaḥ śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chando jyotiṣam iti |
atha parā yayā tad akṣaram adhigamyate || 5 ||

lines.iast: tatrāparā ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvavedaḥ śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chando jyotiṣam iti
lines.deva: तत्रापरा ऋग्वेदो यजुर्वेदः सामवेदोऽथर्ववेदः शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं छन्दो ज्योतिषमिति

lines.iast: atha parā yayā tad akṣaram adhigamyate
lines.deva: अथ परा यया तदक्षरमधिगम्यते

padaccheda.iast: tatra aparā ṛgvedaḥ yajurvedaḥ sāmavedaḥ atharvavedaḥ śikṣā kalpaḥ vyākaraṇam niruktam chandaḥ jyotiṣam iti atha parā yayā tat akṣaram adhigamyate
padaccheda.deva: तत्र अपरा ऋग्वेदः यजुर्वेदः सामवेदः अथर्ववेदः शिक्षा कल्पः व्याकरणम् निरुक्तम् छन्दः ज्योतिषम् इति अथ परा यया तत् अक्षरम् अधिगम्यते

translations.text: Of these the lower is the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, the Atharvaveda, phonetics, ritual, grammar, etymology, metre and astronomy. And the higher is that by which the imperishable is attained.

notes: Śaṅkara: the four Vedas and the six limbs are the lower knowledge. adhigamyate: is attained, for adhi with gam mostly means attaining; and attaining the supreme is not other than knowing it, since the removal of ignorance is itself the attaining of the supreme, nothing else.

Śaṅkara, on an objection: if the higher knowledge stands outside the Ṛgveda and the rest, how can it be higher, or a means to liberation? The law books call the teachings outside the Veda false views, to be rejected as fruitless (Manu 12.95); and the Upaniṣads would fall outside the Veda; while if they are within it, naming them apart is pointless. No: what is meant here by ‘the higher knowledge’ is chiefly the knowing of the imperishable that is to be known from the Upaniṣads, not the mass of words of the Upaniṣads; whereas ‘Veda’ everywhere means the mass of words. Even when the words are learnt, the imperishable is not attained without a further effort, going to a teacher and the rest, and dispassion; so the knowledge of Brahman is named apart, ‘and the higher’.

sanskrit.deva:
यत्तदद्रेश्यमग्राह्यमगोत्रमवर्णमचक्षुःश्रोत्रं तदपाणिपादम् ।
नित्यं विभुं सर्वगतं सुसूक्ष्मं तदव्ययं यद्भूतयोनिं परिपश्यन्ति धीराः ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yat tad adreśyam agrāhyam agotram avarṇam acakṣuḥśrotraṃ tad apāṇipādam |
nityaṃ vibhuṃ sarvagataṃ susūkṣmaṃ tad avyayaṃ yad bhūtayoniṃ paripaśyanti dhīrāḥ || 6 ||

lines.iast: yat tad adreśyam agrāhyam agotram avarṇam acakṣuḥśrotraṃ tad apāṇipādam
lines.deva: यत्तदद्रेश्यमग्राह्यमगोत्रमवर्णमचक्षुःश्रोत्रं तदपाणिपादम्

lines.iast: nityaṃ vibhuṃ sarvagataṃ susūkṣmaṃ tad avyayaṃ yad bhūtayoniṃ paripaśyanti dhīrāḥ
lines.deva: नित्यं विभुं सर्वगतं सुसूक्ष्मं तदव्ययं यद्भूतयोनिं परिपश्यन्ति धीराः

padaccheda.iast: yat tat adreśyam agrāhyam agotram avarṇam acakṣuḥ-śrotram tat apāṇi-pādam nityam vibhum sarvagatam susūkṣmam tat avyayam yat bhūta-yonim paripaśyanti dhīrāḥ
padaccheda.deva: यत् तत् अद्रेश्यम् अग्राह्यम् अगोत्रम् अवर्णम् अचक्षुः-श्रोत्रम् तत् अपाणि-पादम् नित्यम् विभुम् सर्वगतम् सुसूक्ष्मम् तत् अव्ययम् यत् भूत-योनिम् परिपश्यन्ति धीराः

translations.text: That which is invisible, ungraspable, without lineage, without colour, without eye or ear, without hands or feet; eternal, manifold (in all beings), present everywhere, most subtle; that undecaying one which the wise see on every side as the source of beings: (that is the imperishable).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: in an injunction, what is to be done, the agnihotra and the rest, stands apart from knowing the meaning of the sentence, for it needs agent and other factors to be brought together. Here, in the higher knowledge, it is not so: it is complete in the very knowing of the sentence, since there is nothing beyond resting in the knowledge of what the words alone make known. So the mantra describes the higher knowledge through the imperishable and its marks.

Śaṅkara: adreśyam: invisible, beyond reach of all the organs of knowledge, for seeing that goes outward passes through the five senses. agrāhyam: not the object of the organs of action. agotram: gotra is lineage, root; it has no root to which it is joined. avarṇam: without the properties of substance, grossness and the like, or whiteness and the like. acakṣuḥśrotram: since it is called ‘all-knowing’ (1.1.9), it might be thought to work, like those in the round of birth, through eye, ear and the other organs; that is denied (‘he sees without eyes, hears without ears’, Śvetāśvatara 3.19). apāṇipādam: without organs of action. Being neither grasped nor grasping, it is eternal, imperishable. vibhum: it becomes (bhavati) manifold (vi-), as all the kinds of living beings from Brahmā down to plants. sarvagatam: pervading, like space. susūkṣmam: most subtle, being free of sound and the rest, which make space, wind and the other elements each grosser than the one before. avyayam: it does not decay; having no limbs it does not decay as a body loses a limb, nor as a king loses his treasury, nor through its qualities, being without qualities and the self of all. bhūtayoni: the cause of beings, as the earth is of the moving and unmoving. paripaśyanti: see everywhere as the Self of all. dhīrāḥ: the discerning. The knowledge by which such an imperishable is attained is the higher knowledge.

sanskrit.deva:
यथोर्णनाभिः सृजते गृह्णते च यथा पृथिव्यामोषधयः संभवन्ति ।
यथा सतः पुरुषात्केशलोमानि तथाक्षरात्संभवतीह विश्वम् ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yathorṇanābhiḥ sṛjate gṛhṇate ca yathā pṛthivyām oṣadhayaḥ saṃbhavanti |
yathā sataḥ puruṣāt keśalomāni tathākṣarāt saṃbhavatīha viśvam || 7 ||

lines.iast: yathorṇanābhiḥ sṛjate gṛhṇate ca yathā pṛthivyām oṣadhayaḥ saṃbhavanti
lines.deva: यथोर्णनाभिः सृजते गृह्णते च यथा पृथिव्यामोषधयः संभवन्ति

lines.iast: yathā sataḥ puruṣāt keśalomāni tathākṣarāt saṃbhavatīha viśvam
lines.deva: यथा सतः पुरुषात्केशलोमानि तथाक्षरात्संभवतीह विश्वम्

padaccheda.iast: yathā ūrṇanābhiḥ sṛjate gṛhṇate ca yathā pṛthivyām oṣadhayaḥ saṃbhavanti yathā sataḥ puruṣāt keśa-lomāni tathā akṣarāt saṃbhavati iha viśvam
padaccheda.deva: यथा ऊर्णनाभिः सृजते गृह्णते च यथा पृथिव्याम् ओषधयः संभवन्ति यथा सतः पुरुषात् केश-लोमानि तथा अक्षरात् संभवति इह विश्वम्

words.meaning: the hair of head and body

translations.text: As the spider sends forth and takes back (its threads), as plants spring up on the earth, as the hair of head and body grows from a living man, so the universe here comes forth from the imperishable.

notes: Śaṅkara: the imperishable was called the source of beings; how, is shown by examples. The spider, needing no other cause, itself sends out threads not other than its own body, and takes them back into itself; plants, rice and the rest, spring from the earth and are not other than it; hair grows from a living man and is unlike him. So from the imperishable, which needs no other cause, comes forth the whole world in this round of birth and death, both like it and unlike it. Several examples are given to make it easy to grasp.

sanskrit.deva:
तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म ततोऽन्नमभिजायते ।
अन्नात्प्राणो मनः सत्यं लोकाः कर्मसु चामृतम् ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tapasā cīyate brahma tato 'nnam abhijāyate |
annāt prāṇo manaḥ satyaṃ lokāḥ karmasu cāmṛtam || 8 ||

lines.iast: tapasā cīyate brahma tato 'nnam abhijāyate
lines.deva: तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म ततोऽन्नमभिजायते

lines.iast: annāt prāṇo manaḥ satyaṃ lokāḥ karmasu cāmṛtam
lines.deva: अन्नात्प्राणो मनः सत्यं लोकाः कर्मसु चामृतम्

padaccheda.iast: tapasā cīyate brahma tataḥ annam abhijāyate annāt prāṇaḥ manaḥ satyam lokāḥ karmasu ca amṛtam
padaccheda.deva: तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म ततः अन्नम् अभिजायते अन्नात् प्राणः मनः सत्यम् लोकाः कर्मसु च अमृतम्

translations.text: By austerity (by knowledge) Brahman swells; from it food (the unmanifest) is born; from food prāṇa (Hiraṇyagarbha), mind, the true (the five elements), the worlds; and in actions the immortal (their fruit).

notes: Śaṅkara: the mantra states the order in which the world comes forth from Brahman: not all at once, as a fistful of jujube fruit is thrown. tapas: knowledge, the knowing of how to create. cīyate: Brahman, wishing to bring forth the world, swells, as a seed swells into a sprout or a father swells with joy at a son; it grows full with the knowledge and power of creating, sustaining and withdrawing. annam: ‘what is eaten’, the unmanifest, the common cause of all in the round of birth, in the state of being about to be manifested. prāṇa: Hiraṇyagarbha, informed by Brahman's power of knowledge and action, common to the world, the sprout from the seed that is ignorance, desire, action and the elements, the self of the world. manas: what intends, imagines, doubts and decides. satyam: the five elements, space and the rest. lokāḥ: the seven worlds, bhūḥ and the rest, in the order of the cosmic egg. karmasu: in them the actions of men and others, by caste and stage of life; and in actions, as their occasion, the immortal: the fruit of action, called immortal because it does not perish as long as the actions do not perish, even in hundreds of crores of kalpas.

sanskrit.deva:
यः सर्वज्ञः सर्वविद्यस्य ज्ञानमयं तपः ।
तस्मादेतद्ब्रह्म नाम रूपमन्नं च जायते ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavid yasya jñānamayaṃ tapaḥ |
tasmād etad brahma nāma rūpam annaṃ ca jāyate || 9 ||

lines.iast: yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavid yasya jñānamayaṃ tapaḥ
lines.deva: यः सर्वज्ञः सर्वविद्यस्य ज्ञानमयं तपः

lines.iast: tasmād etad brahma nāma rūpam annaṃ ca jāyate
lines.deva: तस्मादेतद्ब्रह्म नाम रूपमन्नं च जायते

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit yasya jñānamayam tapaḥ tasmāt etat brahma nāma rūpam annam ca jāyate
padaccheda.deva: यः सर्वज्ञः सर्ववित् यस्य ज्ञानमयम् तपः तस्मात् एतत् ब्रह्म नाम रूपम् अन्नम् च जायते

translations.text: From him who is all-knowing and knows each thing, whose austerity consists of knowledge, are born this Brahman (Hiraṇyagarbha), name and form, and food.

notes: Śaṅkara: the mantra sums up what was said and leads to what follows. sarvajñaḥ: knowing all in general; sarvavit: knowing all in particular. jñānamayaṃ tapaḥ: his austerity is a form of knowledge, his all-knowing, without effort. etad brahma: the effect described, Brahman called Hiraṇyagarbha. nāma: names such as Devadatta, Yajñadatta; rūpa: forms such as white and blue; anna: food, rice, barley and the like; all born in the order of the previous mantra, so there is no conflict.
